cacheKey.normalizedQuery: story:B-9812 Run the complete root test suite safely in parallel in under five minutes An isolated measurement at commit 58c7cdc showed that root npm test passed all 46 members but took 1688.9 seconds. proofstory-acceptance-rollout, review-incremental-context-smoke, and proofstory-intent-hardening-smoke consumed 79.9 percent of the total. One acceptance cohort case took 26.42 seconds, with about 95.2 percent spent in 26 fresh-process Lattice CLI invocations while Git and build together took less than 0.5 seconds. Implement safe concurrency and eliminate redundant initialization so canonical root npm test completes in less than 300 seconds on each of three consecutive runs from a reproducible clean temporary clone after a same-material packages/main build. Preserve the complete current test membership, deterministic assertions, mutation bites, black-box dist and CLI boundaries, and DONE-required evidence semantics. The target must not be met by deleting tests, silently reducing coverage, moving current required members out of the canonical full suite, concurrently writing an unisolated repository, or converting an initial FAIL or TIMEOUT into PASS through serial retry. Repeated stress iterations may move to an explicit stress layer only when equivalence is proven and the canonical full suite retains deterministic coverage of the same concurrency, ABA, and restoration contracts without weakening gate assurance. CHK-001 Establish a reproducible full-suite performance and coverage baseline Produce machine-readable wall, user, and system timing per root npm test member together with process launch counts, suite membership, assertion and mutation inventories, and failure outcomes. Pin the current 46-member passing baseline and the 1688.9-second reference. Measure only from a clean temporary clone after a same-material packages/main build without polluting the project directory. CHK-002 Define and enforce a resource-isolation contract for concurrent tests Extend the smoke manifest and runner with parallel-safe, exclusive Git common-dir, exclusive fixed port or path, shared runtime lock, and main-write lock classifications. Run tasks concurrently only when isolation is proven. Require unique temporary roots and reliable child cleanup on timeout or interruption. Mechanically serialize conflicting resources, and default unknown classifications to fail closed or serial execution. CHK-003 Eliminate duplicate acceptance rollout cohorts and repeated CLI cold starts Preserve real dist and CLI black-box sentinels and all rollout diagnostics, mutation and restoration checks, reviewer lanes, and quorum assertions. Generate each cohort once, freeze it with a signed digest, and reuse it. Run independent cases concurrently in isolated temporary repositories. Reuse an in-process context or batch entry for matrix checks that do not need repeated process-boundary verification, with explicit equivalence checks against the real CLI path. CHK-004 Reduce incremental-context and intent-hardening long tails without losing race coverage Safely shard independent scenarios and use deterministic seeds or schedules for mixed reviewer writers, ABA, cutoff, and restoration cases. Do not claim equivalence merely by reducing the twenty-iteration loop. If redundant burn-in moves to a stress layer, retain deterministic canonical cases that kill the same mutations and provide an old-versus-new assertion and failure-matrix comparison. CHK-005 Route canonical root npm test through the safe scheduler with complete membership Replace the 46-command npm run serial chain with the resource-aware runner. Add a bidirectional completeness check between the old script inventory and the new manifest so omissions, duplicates, and unexpected skips fail. Preserve focused test diagnostic entries. An initial FAIL or TIMEOUT must remain failed and cannot be masked by automatic serial retry. Parallel execution and jobs=1 must produce equivalent member status and critical evidence. CHK-006 Prove three consecutive sub-five-minute runs and concurrency safety After a same-material build in a clean temporary clone, run canonical root npm test three consecutive times with every run below 300000 milliseconds and every member in the completeness-checked full set passing. Record per-member timing, critical path, worker utilization, and resource-lock wait. Establish jobs=1 result equivalence and use mutations that introduce shared-path conflicts, timeout, child leakage, and test failure to prove resource locking, cleanup, and fail-closed behavior. DONE-required receipts must still accurately record canonical root npm test. story intake repro-first stale-doc truth-first playbook runtime memory non-authoritative

devMemory.summary: A/B measurement of B-cee5 prompt stopgap: agents deviate from scan mandates either way, and no mechanical read-evidence exists to detect it.
devMemory.lesson: Old full-scan prompt: the agent silently disobeyed (read 1 of 111 decisions docs, no audit trail) yet asserted complete coverage — in production such deviation is invisible, so coverage claims under the old prompt were unverifiable; when agents DO obey, the 2.4MB corpus costs ~600k+ input tokens (the original exhaustion). New bounded contract produced equivalent review quality (same load-bearing gaps and same spec-contradiction OQ) at 74.8k vs 79.3k tokens with a recorded enumeration + candidate basis + explicit non-escalation reason. Core gap remaining: what a reviewer actually READ is self-reported prose, not evidence — there is no read manifest bound to scope_check_save/review_pass_set and no transcript-derived read log, so future before/after comparisons and compliance proofs (detecting unrecorded full scans) have no ground truth. Prompt-layer stopgap is instructional only; proof needs mechanical read evidence.
devMemory.reusePrompt: reviewer read evidence, scan compliance, token stopgap measurement, read manifest, scanEscalationReason audit, B-cee5 effect

devMemory.summary: A story whose diff includes package.json turns every later main merge into related drift: quorum, delivery-check, and review passes all stale and force a full re-review round.
devMemory.lesson: storyFilesHash covers the story diff file set. package.json is in that set whenever the story wires npm scripts (or gets scope-acknowledged version bumps), and DONE auto-bumps touch package.json on every merge to main — so any sibling story landing first changes YOUR story-owned material. Cost in B-3b05: one extra TEST->DEV->REVIEW round (4 reviewer lanes re-pass), fresh quorum_submit, fresh delivery_check_set. Mitigations: close stories promptly once quorum is bound; expect and budget the round-4 re-review when parallel stories share package.json; command-backed evidence must be actually re-run (refresh_stale refuses to rebind it silently).
devMemory.reusePrompt: stale delivery-check materialHash mismatch after merge / review assurance floor local rounds 0 after mergeMain / related drift package.json

devMemory.summary: Run quorum_submit during REVIEW, before advancing to TEST, once all active lanes have current-round passes.
devMemory.lesson: quorum_submit satisfies the 3x2 review-assurance floor by converting CURRENT-round signed review passes from ALL active reviewer lanes into host verdict records (hostA=claude-cli hostB=codex-cli); it refuses to fabricate. review_run_start/review_pass_set are REVIEW-phase-only, so advancing to TEST first (the round-2+ gate needs only >=1 receipt) strands the other lanes without a write path and forces a TEST->DEV->REVIEW round-trip to mint fresh passes in a new round. Correct order: all lanes pass in current round -> quorum_submit -> story_advance TEST.
devMemory.reusePrompt: review assurance floor blocked / quorum_submit missing current pass lanes / review_pass_set not available in TEST

devMemory.summary: Parallel reviewers' destructive dist bite-tests on a shared story worktree race each other; serialize them or use an isolated worktree copy.
devMemory.lesson: Destructive compiled-dist experiments (remove a registry name, run smoke, restore) must not overlap other reviewers using the same dist: a concurrently patched dist yields spurious FAIL observations. Either serialize the destructive step after all read-only lanes finish, or do what the round-2 quality lane did: build a scratch git worktree copy and bite there. Byte-restore and re-run the smoke afterward to prove the shared dist is intact.
devMemory.reusePrompt: dist bite test race, shared worktree destructive experiment, spurious smoke failure during review

devMemory.summary: ProofStory DONE shrinkage detector is a regex over summary text; shrinkage-flavored wording about neighboring items falsely blocks DONE.
devMemory.lesson: evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence (core/proofstory.ts ~1582) flags unconfirmed_single_outcome_shrinkage via a regex matching out of scope, follow-up, not covered, deferred, excluded, partial, narrower etc. in the DONE summary. Describing a NEIGHBORING issue as out of this story scope / spun off as a follow-up in summary limitations trips the gate even when the story delivered everything promised. Fix by rephrasing (the sibling item is a different artifact owned by its own task; this story delivered fully) via summary_set, not by recording a false scope_shrinkage_decision_set.
devMemory.reusePrompt: unconfirmed_single_outcome_shrinkage / DONE summary appears narrower than original snapshot
